metadata.case_name: LING MAN KUEN v. CHOW CHAN MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: assistant engineer responsible for the maintenance and inspection of lifts and escalators (training to be a Safety Officer)

source:
"Right forehead and left temporal, face was injured. There was no loss of consciousness or convulsion after accident, but he had vomiting for 3 times later. He complained of distending headache and blurred vision and epistasis. The epistasis was stopped spontaneously. He also had right should and chest wall pain. On examination, Glasgow coma scale was full. There was 1 cm bruising over right forehead. Tenderness over left temporal region, left chest wall and right shoulder. . .

Headache subsided with symptomatic treatment. CT brain showed no fracture or intracranial haematoma.

X-ray skull, face, chest and right shoulder also showed no fractures. He was discharged on 01.11.2003. . .The diagnosis was minor head injury and symptomatic treatment was given according to patient’s condition."
The medical officers of the Neurosurgery Department of the United Christian Hospital diagnosed him to have post-concussion syndrome.
